text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - Shares closed higher as index heavyweights British Telecom and Glaxo gained and hopes grew that Wall Street had seen the worst of its recent correction. Rising utility stocks also propelled the market higher amid hopes that the "windfall" tax planned by Labour if it wins the May 1 election will be less harsh than previously feared. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,313.2, up 20.9 points, or 0.49 percent.

FRANKFURT - Germany's DAX index ended bourse marginally lower, shedding some of the gains from the DAX's recent recovery, after Wall Street ended lower overnight and the dollar lost ground against the mark. Dealers said that volumes in the market were very low over the session and that even small orders were able to move the market appreciably. The DAX closed at 3,351.49 points, down 7.97 points. In post-bourse trade the IBIS DAX index fell 12.18 to 3,352.58.

PARIS - Equities in Paris finished lower after an indecisive day in which the CAC index drifted in a 21-point range. The CAC dipped below 2,600 but recovered to trade above this support level. Traders said the market lacked big themes to drive the index higher and slim hopes of a rate cut were snuffed out when the Bank of France left rates unchanged at a money market tender. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 9.58 points at 2,607.97.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended a volatile session mixed to lower. Dealers said trade was quiet as investors waited for Friday's CPI and retail data from the U.S. The Broad SPI was down 2.90 points to 2,926.88.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended with losses as buying of bank shares on news of a business tie-up between Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) and Bankers Trust New York Corp waned in the afternoon session, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average lost 217.62 points to 17,485.75.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed lower for the first time in four days, as inflation and property market fears undermined sentiment, brokers said. The Hang Seng Index was down 67.98 points at 12,358.7.

SYDNEY - A rangebound Australian share market captured only light gains by the close after mixed finishes in offshore markets dampened the buying enthusiasm seen on Wednesday afternoon. The All Ordinaries index added 3.7 points to 2,392.9.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended a second lacklustre day just weaker, weathering blows from losses on Wall Street overnight and falls on the local rand and bond market. Dealers said that although trading turnover on the day was above average, with deals worth around 760 million rand taking place, this was boosted by a small number of large transactions. The rand touched its weakest level in five weeks on Thursday, sliding to a worst day's position of 4.4735 bid, taking the bond market down with it. The 100 percent all-share index finished down only 3.4 points at 7,045.1 after the industrial index slipped 6.2 at 8,243.7. On the gold board, activity was equally subdued with the index adding 1.9 points to 1,311.1.
